# Yantra (यन्त्र)

> A personal developer control plane: one interface over the workspaces, AI coding agents and
> machines on a Tailscale mesh. Ask for a workspace and it picks a machine, opens the tmux session,
> and resumes the agent. Rust daemon, CLI and per-machine agent; TypeScript web UI. Personal-scale
> and deliberately so — its niche is pre-existing, personally-owned, heterogeneous machines that must
> never be destroyed, which is the case Coder and DevPod cannot represent.

**Read `tracker.md` first.** It is the single source of truth for project state, and it wins over
anything else — including this file — when they disagree.

Each crate carries its own `CLAUDE.md`, `tracker.md`, `llms.txt` and `README.md`. Start at the crate
you are changing rather than reading the root documents end to end. **The invariants live in the
crate trackers** — 48 non-obvious rules, numbered to I-51, most earned by a bug that presented as
something else, and 35 of them in `yantra-core`. They are the highest-value thing in the repo.

## Start here

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): project state — milestones, open tasks, decisions, open questions, risks, and an index of where the invariants live.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): how to work in this repo — think before coding, surgical changes, and what "verification" means here (a real sshd and a real tmux, never a mock).
- [README.md](README.md): what Yantra is, for a human — install, usage, the workspace schema.
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the structure, the `up` sequence, the trust boundaries and where the live risks sit, as rendered diagrams. The fastest way to orient.

## Crates

- [yantra-core](crates/yantra-core/llms.txt): all the orchestration — ssh, tmux, agents, inventory, workspaces. Never prints, never exits. This is where nearly all the code is.
- [yantra](crates/yantra/llms.txt): the CLI. Renders and chooses exit codes; decides nothing.
- [yantrad](crates/yantrad/llms.txt): the daemon. An axum server binding only this machine's Tailscale addresses: a read-only JSON API over a background snapshot, five writes (`POST /heartbeat`, and `new`/`up`/`down`/`resume` per workspace, authorised by Tailscale identity), and the dashboard itself.
- [yantra-agent](crates/yantra-agent/llms.txt): the per-machine heartbeat — seven probes, a 10 s loop and a hand-written POST. Install is M7's.

## Decisions

Accepted ADRs are immutable. If one is wrong, propose a superseding ADR — do not quietly build
something else.

- [docs/adr/](docs/adr/): fifteen of them. The ones that constrain most code are [0005](docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md) (library crate), [0006](docs/adr/0006-ssh-exec-transport.md) (ssh transport), [0009](docs/adr/0009-machine-names-are-ssh-destinations.md) (machine names) and [0011](docs/adr/0011-claude-code-runs-as-a-tui-in-tmux.md) (the agent is a TUI).
- [docs/research/](docs/research/): ten dated research notes across seven topics. Evidence as of their access date, not eternal truth — re-verify anything version-sensitive.

## Optional

- [docs/development.md](docs/development.md): local setup and daily commands.
- [docs/machines.md](docs/machines.md): the actual fleet this is developed against.
- [docs/vision.md](docs/vision.md): the long-range shape, including the hardware panel.
- [docs/session-log.md](docs/session-log.md): one line per working session, append-only. Newest last.
- [docs/archive/m0-m1.md](docs/archive/m0-m1.md): closed milestones M0 and M1. History, not current state.
- [docs/archive/m2-m3.md](docs/archive/m2-m3.md): closed milestones M2 and M3, with the evidence behind each task.
